# meshes.library: Deform

```plato
//==
// # Meshes
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Deformation body for the attributed mesh
//  - Bodies for the unwelded face arrays
//  - The IFace corner surface and its derived loop walks
//  - Derived functionality for meshable and sampled geometry
//  - Interface obligations of the indexed surface meshes
//  - What the layered mesh vocabulary derives for free
//  - Deformation bodies for line sets and bare point clouds
//  - Deformation body for the partitioned mesh
//  - Derived functionality for mesh connectivity
//  - Deformation bodies for the volumetric meshes

library Meshes
{
    //==
    // # Deformation body for the attributed mesh
    //
    // The IDeformable3D obligation of RichMesh3D (`meshes.types.plato`): the
    // underlying triangle mesh is deformed and every attribute channel is carried
    // unchanged. Positions are the only point-typed data the type holds;
    // direction-valued channels (vector, tangent) are NOT re-derived — after a
    // non-rigid mapping the caller decides whether to recompute them, the same
    // stale-normal contract every DCC deformer follows.

    // The IDeformable3D obligation: the mesh deformed, every channel unchanged.
    Deform(self: RichMesh3D, mapping: Function1<Point3D, Point3D>): RichMesh3D
        => (self.Mesh.Deform(mapping),
            self.NumberChannels,
            self.IntegerChannels,
            self.VectorChannels,
            self.UvChannels,
            self.ColorChannels,
            self.TangentChannels);

    // The IMesh3D obligation: the geometry without its attribute channels.
    ToTriangleMesh(self: RichMesh3D): TriangleMesh3D
        => self.Mesh;

    //==
    // # Bodies for the unwelded face arrays
    //
    // The interface obligations of `TriangleArray3D` / `QuadArray3D`
    // (`meshes.types.plato`). `Points` flattens the faces in authored order,
    // which is what makes the index table of `ToTriangleMesh` the identity: corner k
    // of face i is position (arity * i + k). `Bounds` comes free from `IPointSet3D`
    // (`geometry.library.plato`) and is tight, since every stored point
    // lies on the geometry.

    //==
    // # TriangleArray3D

    // Every corner position, three per triangle, in face order.
    Points(a: TriangleArray3D): Array<Point3D>
        => a.Triangles.FlatMap(t => t.Points);

    // The IMesh3D obligation. No welding: positions are the flattened corners
    // and the faces index them consecutively, so a mesh with shared vertices
    // requires a separate weld pass.
    ToTriangleMesh(a: TriangleArray3D): TriangleMesh3D
        => (a.Points,
            a.Triangles.Count.MapRange(i =>
                TriangleFace(VertexIndex(3 * i), VertexIndex(3 * i + 1), VertexIndex(3 * i + 2))));

    // Applies the mapping to every corner of every triangle.
    // Constructed explicitly: the single field is an Array, and a C# backend cannot declare the
    // implicit conversion for an interface-typed field (CS0552), so a bare array body has
    // nothing to convert through.
    Deform(a: TriangleArray3D, mapping: Function1<Point3D, Point3D>): TriangleArray3D
        => TriangleArray3D(a.Triangles.Map(t => t.Deform(mapping)));

    // The PrimitiveCollection3D obligation: the stored faces themselves.
    Primitives(a: TriangleArray3D): Array<Triangle3D>
        => a.Triangles;

    //==
    // # QuadArray3D

    // Every corner position, four per quad, in face order.
    Points(a: QuadArray3D): Array<Point3D>
        => a.Quads.FlatMap(q => q.Points);

    // The two triangles of one quad, split on the A-C diagonal, indexing the
    // flattened corner positions of that quad.
    QuadTriangleFaces(a: QuadArray3D, quad: Integer): Array<TriangleFace>
    {
        var b = 4 * quad;
        return [TriangleFace(VertexIndex(b), VertexIndex(b + 1), VertexIndex(b + 2)),
                TriangleFace(VertexIndex(b), VertexIndex(b + 2), VertexIndex(b + 3))];
    }

    // The IMesh3D obligation: two triangles per quad over the flattened
    // corners.
    ToTriangleMesh(a: QuadArray3D): TriangleMesh3D
        => (a.Points,
            a.Quads.Count.MapRange(i => i).FlatMap(i => a.QuadTriangleFaces(i)));

    // Applies the mapping to every corner of every quad.
    // Explicit construction, same reason as the TriangleArray3D twin above.
    Deform(a: QuadArray3D, mapping: Function1<Point3D, Point3D>): QuadArray3D
        => QuadArray3D(a.Quads.Map(q => q.Deform(mapping)));

    // The PrimitiveCollection3D obligation: the stored faces themselves.
    Primitives(a: QuadArray3D): Array<Quad3D>
        => a.Quads;

    //==
    // # The IFace corner surface and its derived loop walks
    //
    // Bodies for the `IFace` interface (`meshes.concepts.plato`): the Count/At
    // obligations of the two fixed-arity face records (`meshes.types.plato`), and the
    // loop vocabulary derived from them — edges, membership, and the fan
    // triangulation that fixes the A-C diagonal split of a quad in code rather
    // than prose. The undirected-edge census helpers at the bottom serve the
    // IMeshElementCounts obligations of the indexed meshes
    //.

    //==
    // # TriangleFace — the IIndexable<VertexIndex> obligations.

    // The arity of a triangle face.
    Count(self: TriangleFace): Integer
        => 3;

    // The index-th corner's vertex index. Corners do not wrap: an index
    // outside [0, 3) reads the corner array, which refuses it, so an
    // off-by-one is an error instead of a silent read of C.
    At(self: TriangleFace, index: Integer): VertexIndex
        => index == 0 ? self.A : (index == 1 ? self.B : (index == 2 ? self.C : self.Vertices[index]));

    // The three corner vertex indices in winding order.
    Vertices(self: TriangleFace): Array<VertexIndex>
        => [self.A, self.B, self.C];

    //==
    // # QuadFace — the IIndexable<VertexIndex> obligations.

    // The arity of a quadrilateral face.
    Count(self: QuadFace): Integer
        => 4;

    // The index-th corner's vertex index. Corners do not wrap: an index
    // outside [0, 4) reads the corner array, which refuses it, so an
    // off-by-one is an error instead of a silent read of D.
    At(self: QuadFace, index: Integer): VertexIndex
        => index == 0 ? self.A : (index == 1 ? self.B : (index == 2 ? self.C : (index == 3 ? self.D : self.Vertices[index])));

    // The four corner vertex indices in winding order.
    Vertices(self: QuadFace): Array<VertexIndex>
        => [self.A, self.B, self.C, self.D];
```
